description: Group B - Trust & safety. B1 secret/credential redaction across overlay log/toasts/captions AND transcript detail strings and any logs, using the src/redact.ts util from FEAT-001. B2 human-in-the-loop confirmation hook via MCP elicitation (opt-in) tied to an amber 'awaiting confirmation' overlay state, preserving refuse-by-default when confirmation is not wired. B3 opt-in extension of the destructive guard to Assist tools (default OFF). Depends on FEAT-001 (config + redact) and FEAT-002 (loop changes should be layered cleanly).
steps: B1 redaction: thread the set of secret VALUES the loop typed into the run. In loop.ts, when a TYPE_TEXT/FILL_FORM fills a field whose control looks secret (use redactValueForField's field-secret test on control.type/name), record the ACTUAL value into an in-run `secrets` string set, but build the StepRecord.detail and the value shown via redactText(detail, [...secrets]) so the transcript `detail` and any recorded `value`/`fields[].value` render masked (mask the value in the StepRecord too: keep executing with the real value, but store the masked form in record.value / record.fields[].value). Ensure the Narrator's log/toast/caption/status calls pass their strings through redactText([...secrets]) before display so nothing secret reaches the overlay. Gate all masking behind config.redactSecrets (thread as RunGoalOptions.redactSecrets, default true); when false, behavior is unchanged. Also mask in renderRunResult if needed (it renders record.value/fields which are already masked, so verify). The REAL value must still be typed into the field (do not weaken automation).

B2 confirmation hook: add an opt-in confirmation path so that when the destructive-form guard would refuse an Autopilot auto-submit CLICK, and config.confirmDestructive is true AND a confirmation callback is available, the loop requests inline human approval instead of immediately refusing. Define a `ConfirmFn = (prompt: string) => Promise<boolean>` injected via RunGoalOptions.confirm. When the guard refuses and confirm is present and confirmDestructive is on: set overlay to a NEW amber 'awaiting confirmation' presentation (reuse setState('uncertain') + a clear status/toast like 'About to click "Delete account" - approve?'), await confirm(prompt); if approved, proceed with the CLICK (record a note 'approved via confirmation'); if refused, keep the existing blocked behavior (record BLOCKED with the guard reason). When confirm is absent or confirmDestructive is off, preserve the EXISTING refuse-by-default fail-safe exactly. In src/server.ts wire the real confirm via server.server.elicitInput(...) (SDK 1.30.1) behind a lazy check of the client's elicitation capability, mirroring how sample is wired for sampling; if the client lacks elicitation, confirm resolves to false (refuse). Keep all of this non-throwing.

B3 assist-tool destructive guard (opt-in, default OFF): add config.assistDestructiveGuard (from FEAT-001, LAYA_ASSIST_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD default false) to ToolContext and thread it from server.ts. In src/tools/click.ts, when assistDestructiveGuard is true, before clicking, capture the current snapshot, build a minimal PageState, resolve the target to a Control, and run checkDestructiveSubmit; if it refuses, return a textResult error surfacing the reason (do NOT click) instead of proceeding. When the flag is false (default) behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (no snapshot, no guard). Keep the change scoped to click.ts (the primary destructive Assist action) as the required example; note in code/README that other Assist tools remain unguarded by design.

Update README Safety-guards section to document B1 (redaction, LAYA_REDACT_SECRETS default true), B2 (LAYA_CONFIRM_DESTRUCTIVE default false, elicitation-based inline approval, amber awaiting-confirmation state, refuse-by-default preserved), and B3 (LAYA_ASSIST_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD default false). Add the three env vars to the Configuration reference table.

Add tests. test/redaction-loop.test.ts (real headless chromium): drive a login fixture with a password field via the loop; assert the transcript detail/value for the password step renders the masked token and NOT the real password, while the live page input actually received the real password value (assert via page.locator(...).inputValue()). test/confirmation.test.ts (unit + loop): with a fake confirm returning true, the destructive CLICK proceeds (outcome not blocked, page mutated) and a note records approval; with confirm returning false OR confirm absent, the run stays blocked and the page is NOT mutated (reuse delete-account.html). test additions in test/safety.test.ts or a new file for B3: browser_click with assistDestructiveGuard=true refuses a 'Delete account' target (isError, reason surfaced, no navigation), and with the flag false (default) clicks normally.
acceptance_criteria: A password/secret value typed by the loop appears masked (bullet token) in the StepRecord.detail, StepRecord.value/fields, overlay log/toast/caption, and renderRunResult output, while the real value is still typed into the field (verified via inputValue()).

With confirmDestructive on and a confirm callback that approves, an otherwise-refused destructive CLICK proceeds and is recorded as approved; with confirm refusing or absent, the run stays blocked and the page is not mutated (existing fail-safe preserved).
With assistDestructiveGuard=true, browser_click refuses a destructive target and does not click; with the flag false (default) browser_click behaves exactly as before.
All new LAYA_ env vars are parsed once in config.ts and documented in the README config table + Safety-guards section.
No secrets appear in any log/detail/overlay output when redactSecrets is on.
verification: Run `npx vitest run test/redaction-loop.test.ts test/confirmation.test.ts` and confirm B1/B2 assertions pass headless.
Run `npx vitest run test/safety.test.ts` and confirm B3 (assist guard opt-in) and existing safety tests pass.
Run `npm run test` and `npm run typecheck` and confirm the full suite passes with the 3 pre-existing skips intact.
